doc: world/history-ui.md is canonical for behavior + copy. This file is the machine-readable archive: the spectator layer of the canonical ledger, one day-object per block day. Event schema is feed.json's, extended with `day` (inherited from the day key), `mentions`, and the `rumor` kind. The archive is FREE — it shows exactly what a spectator could have observed live, nothing more. Homes are walls; secrets are absent by construction (there is no field that could carry one).

day_schema.who: optional character id (C1–C8, A01–A20) or player handle on request events
day_schema.mentions: optional array of character ids named in the text — makes per-character history structural, not string-matched
day_schema.req: optional, request events: shared request id — every lifecycle event of one paid intervention carries it; archive detail views group the status trail on it (same contract as feed.json)
day_schema.src: rumor events only — where the talk was overheard (a venue id or 'the block')
day_schema.outcome: rumor events only — { state: 'debunked'|'faded'|'stood', note } filled in when the talk resolves; null while open
day_schema.thread: optional array of thread ids — archive-layer arrangement metadata only: chains already-public events a spectator could have followed; never carries information the events don't

rumor_kind: word on the block — talk overheard in public, shown UNCONFIRMED, never sourced to a named character, may only ever distort events that were already public; a rumor that happens to be true about a secret is a bug, not content
coverage_rules: the archive holds the SPECTATOR layer only — identical scope to the live wire, replayed
uncovered stretches render as honest gaps ('off the feed'), not interpolated filler
request text in the archive is the same screened text the live wire showed; denied bodies were never written
rumor entries carry no author — attribution is a place ('overheard near Malik's'), never a name
admin/request attribution is preserved verbatim from the live feed — the archive does not sanitize history
today's day-object exists but ends at the last completed hour — the archive does not write the present

archive_ui.doc: world v20 — the full history surface (world/archive.html, spec world/archive-ui.md). history.html remains the lightweight day-browser variant.
archive_ui.data_source: live: __aiBridge.gsWireDays() + gsWireArchiveDay(dateStr) (game-v6) emitting day_schema objects; demo: this file's `days` verbatim. Badge reads 'live archive' / 'demo archive'.

views.day: one block day — hour-density strip, kind filters, search, honest 'off the feed' gaps; today capped at last completed hour
views.person: cross-day trail via who + mentions[] — structural only; 'public whereabouts only'; never infers uncovered time
views.venue: cross-day record per venue id; 'block' includes street-level venue:null events
views.word: the rumor board — every rumor event with place-source + outcome tally (open/debunked/faded/stood)
views.ledger: every request + admin event, attributed verbatim — payer handle, status, declared credits, compensation. The archive does not sanitize who paid.

permalinks: #e=<id> resolves the record; day derived from the d<MMDD> id prefix
honesty: projections add no information — person/venue/ledger views rearrange rows, never extend scope
rumor outcome writes are append-only corrections on the archived event; the rumor entry is never rewritten
no affordance on any archive view touches the world — no comments, votes, annotations, or reach-ins

archive_ui_v34.doc: world v34 — The Archive v3: threads (named chains of already-public events), a per-payer lens on the ledger, whole-record search from the day view, and a copyable day transcript. All projections — arrangement only, zero new information.

views_added.threads: named storylines across days, built from event.thread tags; a thread only ever chains events that were already public. Open state derives from member events (open rumor / open request). #v=threads&th=<id>
views_added.ledger_payer_lens: payer chips on the ledger — one handle per chip, verbatim; filtering shows that payer's request/admin events and declared-credit total. Attribution stays unsanitized.
views_added.whole_record_search: day-view search gains a 'whole record' scope — matches render grouped by day via the same trail renderer; hits are still only display text + resolved names + venue names + mentions
views_added.day_transcript: 'copy transcript' on the day header emits the day as plain text (HH:MM + kind + text, rumors prefixed 'unconfirmed —'); free, unstyled, exactly what the page shows

honesty: thread labels are archive chrome, not narration — a thread asserts nothing beyond its member rows
transcript copy carries the source badge (live/demo) in its header line
payer totals are computed from attrs.credits only where declared — undeclared stays undeclared
